hook: Stevie Wonder Unearths *4* Lost Songs After 50 Years
dek: Stevie Wonder surprise dropped 4 unreleased tracks from his 1976 classic.

slides.label: What Happened
slides.text: Stevie Wonder surprise dropped a new EP with *four unreleased songs* from his 1976 sessions.

slides.label: The Songs
slides.text: The EP includes *“It’s Easier,”* “My Life Story of Love,” “I Can See the Sun in Late December,” and “I’m Into Livin’.”

slides.label: Why Now
slides.text: He held them back for *50 years*, releasing them now ahead of his anniversary tour.

slides.label: The Timing
slides.text: The EP dropped at *4:54 a.m. PDT*, the exact time the original 1976 sessions wrapped.

slides.label: The Legacy
slides.text: *Songs in the Key of Life* is diamond certified and ranked #4 on Rolling Stone's all time list.

slides.label: Who Played
slides.text: Wonder played most instruments himself, joined by bassist Nathan Watts and backup singers *Thelma Houston* and *Deneice Williams*.

slides.label: What's Next
slides.text: Wonder kicks off a *world tour* Oct. 13 in Birmingham, England, wrapping Dec. 19 in Los Angeles.

slides.label: Why It Matters
slides.text: For Black artists, owning your vault and choosing your own timeline is real *ownership*, not just nostalgia.

caption_instagram:
Stevie Wonder just gave us four gifts we didn't know we needed.

Fifty years after Songs in the Key of Life dropped, Wonder surprise-released an EP with four unreleased tracks from those same sessions: “It’s Easier,” “My Life Story of Love,” “I Can See the Sun in Late December,” and “I’m Into Livin’.” He held onto them for half a century, saving them for the right moment.

That moment is now. The EP landed at 4:54 a.m. PDT, the exact time the original sessions wrapped back in 1976, an inside joke among Wonder and his band turned tribute. He's also gearing up for a world tour this fall to celebrate the album's anniversary.

Rolling Stone ranked the original album #4 on its Greatest Albums list. Fifty years later, it's still teaching us what mastery and patience look like.

Stevie Wonder just dropped four songs he's been sitting on for 50 years.

They came from the Songs in the Key of Life sessions back in 1976, an album Rolling Stone ranked the 4th greatest of all time. Wonder never added them to the record, but he says they were part of what he was feeling while he made it. Now, ahead of his anniversary world tour this fall, he's finally letting the world hear them.

The EP even dropped at 4:54 a.m. PDT, the exact minute the original sessions ended half a century ago.

Fifty years after releasing Songs in the Key of Life, one of the most celebrated albums in music history, Wonder surprise-dropped an EP of four unreleased tracks from those original sessions. He'd held onto the songs for decades, choosing to release them now alongside a world tour marking the album's anniversary.

According to Rolling Stone, the album is diamond certified and sits at Number Four on the outlet's list of the 500 Greatest Albums of All Time. The new EP was timed to the exact minute the original sessions wrapped in 1976, a small detail that says a lot about intention and control over your own story.

For creators and founders building something meant to last, this is a reminder that timing, patience, and ownership of your work matter as much as the output itself.
